slides.title: 5 kitchen fire myths to drop before Thanksgiving dinner

slides.myth: Thanksgiving is just another day in the kitchen.
slides.fact: It's the No. 1 day of the year for home cooking fires in the U.S., with about 1,450 reported on Thanksgiving 2023 alone.

slides.myth: It's fine to step away from the stove for a minute.
slides.fact: Unattended cooking is the leading cause of home cooking fires. Leaving the kitchen, even briefly? Turn the burner off first.

slides.myth: Throw flour on a grease fire to smother it.
slides.fact: Never use flour or water. Slide a lid over the pan, turn off the heat and leave the lid on until it cools.

slides.myth: Open the oven to see how bad the fire is.
slides.fact: Keep the door shut and turn off the heat. Closed, the fire runs out of air. Opening it feeds the flames.

slides.myth: A turkey fryer is fine on the porch or in the garage.
slides.fact: Fry outdoors in the open, away from walls and anything that burns. Thaw and dry the bird first: a frozen or wet one makes the oil spatter.
